title: Anglo-Zanzibar War
summary: On 27 August 1896, after the death of Sultan Hamad, British warships shelled the palace at Zanzibar to remove Khalid ibn Barghash, who had proclaimed himself sultan. Atlas Obscura reports about 500 Zanzibaris killed or wounded and one British seaman injured; EBSCO says about five hundred defenders were killed. Britain installed its own candidate, Hamoud ibn Muhammad.

uncertainty.note: Atlas Obscura gives 9:00 am on 27 August; EBSCO gives August 1896 for the sultan's death and does not date the bombardment.

as_recorded.value: During the previous month, Zanzibar's Sultan Hamid ibn Thuwain had died.

where.modern_name: Stone Town, Zanzibar City, Tanzania (proxy pin: UNESCO coordinates for the Stone Town of Zanzibar; the shelled palace lay on the waterfront)
where.historical_name: Zanzibar town, Sultanate of Zanzibar (British protected state)

importance.justification: EBSCO links the intervention to the 1897 decree abolishing slavery in Zanzibar; Atlas Obscura describes it as a famously short war.

sources.title: World Heritage List syndication (XML): entry id_number 173, Stone Town of Zanzibar, geolocation -6.16306, 39.18917
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre (syndication dataset)

reviewer_note: Duration is not stated in the summary: Atlas Obscura says how many minutes it lasted is uncertain, and I could not open History Today (blocked). Casualty figures kept as attributed: "about 500 killed or wounded" (Atlas Obscura) vs "about five hundred defenders" killed (EBSCO). Pin is a proxy (centre of Stone Town per UNESCO), not the palace itself. EBSCO has no day-level date; the day comes from Atlas Obscura alone.
